findings.summary: Action–domain–responder (ADR) is a web-oriented software architectural pattern proposed as a refinement of MVC. It structures handling of HTTP requests into three sequential components: the action captures request input and invokes the domain, the domain contains business logic and may modify state via storage interaction, and the responder exclusively builds the HTTP response using the domain's output. ADR differs from MVC by enforcing strict unidirectional control flow, separating action classes from responder logic, and preventing the domain from being modified by a view layer.

mechanisms.title: Request handling flow
mechanisms.explanation: The action component receives HTTP request details (URL and method), passes input to the domain, and upon domain completion, hands control exclusively to the responder. This serial flow mirrors HTTP request-response cycles more closely than MVC's controller-view cycle.

mechanisms.title: Domain encapsulation and responder output generation
mechanisms.explanation: The domain component owns business logic and state modification, interacting with storage as needed. It receives information only from the action and passes output solely to the responder, which is solely responsible for constructing the full HTTP response, including selecting any view or template system.

unknowns: How domain state modification interacts with concurrent HTTP requests
Whether the responder component supports pluggable view systems beyond those explicitly documented
